minutes.headline: Sewer Commission cut the A&G Crossroads non-compliance fine to a lower paid-now amount and sent its ARPA package to Selectmen.
minutes.summary: The commission voted to forward its ARPA funding request (manholes and pump stations) to the Select Board for a June 6 presentation, and reduced the A&G Crossroads grease-interceptor fine after a hearing with the owner's representative. It also voted to cut the assistant business manager position to under 24 hours and non-benefited. Other items were informational: the Woodard & Curran I&I report, IMA negotiations with Leominster, capital planning and SCADA, and a jetting truck rental.

public_comment.topic: No public comment at the opening; announcements were thanks to Jane for working the polls and introduction of visitor Mike Mackin.
Visitor Mike Mackin said he enjoyed the discussions and is interested in infrastructure and the environment; the chair said appointment would require the Select Board.

votes.motion: Approve minutes from 4/11 through 4/30 (as heard '4 11 till 8 30')
Send the ARPA proposal to the Select Board as soon as possible for review
Reduce the A&G Crossroads non-compliance fine to 750 from 2525, paid immediately and in full
Change assistant business manager position from 24 hours benefited to 20 hours or less

budget_items.what_was_said: Business manager said the request is for manhole repairs in the Electric Ave, Mass Ave and other areas, with itemized costs from 2015 inflated by an escalator.
A second component requests funding for pump replacements, panel upgrades, motor shafts and generators at several stations.
Fee stood at the initial non-compliance fee plus daily fines for missing pump-out reports; the commission discussed reducing it.
figures_as_heard: two thousand four hundred and seventy five dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: Members settled around an amount meant to cover the manager's staff time and send a message.
Estimated current-year capital expenditures for cranes, block heaters, panels and a dialer are covered by the existing budget; SCADA at two stations was floated for next year.
Budget adds money for jetting; DPW director found renting a jetter truck far cheaper than hiring a contractor, though labor and consultant hours add cost.
Position reduced from a benefited 24-hour post to under 20 hours non-benefited; change requires collective bargaining.

decisions.decision: Add to the ARPA presentation that funds may be used to eliminate/line manholes where possible; presentation set for Tuesday June 6, 7:30-8:30.
Commission gave a green light (no vote) for the manager to draft a letter supporting removal of the testing component from the draft NPDES permit, due June 5.
Dave McDonald to meet with town counsel about whether IMA negotiations can be discussed in executive session; negotiations to proceed via a non-quorum group.
Manager to ask to be involved in the Select Board's grant application for the Leominster-Shirley corridor development; members voiced support.
Manager to contact Jake Fleming for manhole lining information; idea of a joint session with Leominster by Zoom was agreed.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to send its ARPA funding request, covering manhole repairs and pump station work, to the Select Board for review.
After a hearing with the owner's representative, the commission voted to reduce the A&G Crossroads non-compliance fine, payable immediately and in full.
The commission voted to change the assistant business manager post from a benefited 24-hour job to 20 hours or less.
Members gave a no-vote green light for a letter supporting removal of the testing component from the draft NPDES permit.
Leominster IMA negotiations were referred to a member meeting with town counsel on whether they can be discussed in executive session.

why_it_matters: The ARPA request, if the Select Board takes it up, would put federal pandemic-relief money toward sewer repairs that would otherwise fall on sewer rates.
The position change touches the sewer department's payroll and benefits costs, and the minutes say it requires collective bargaining.
The IMA negotiations with Leominster and the draft permit's testing component both bear on future treatment costs and permit terms, though no figures were settled here.
watch_next: Tuesday June 6, 7:30-8:30: the ARPA presentation to the Select Board.
June 5: the deadline for comments on the draft NPDES permit.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all three votes in substance and on nearly every dollar figure; the differences are mostly caption misspellings of names. The one point to check is the Assistant Business Manager vote, where ours says "20 hours or less" and the town's says "under 20 hours".
